Revenue has two lines with very different margins: manufacturing (sheet-metal, chassis, exhaust, polymer, suspension and other parts; 81% of FY26 revenue, 13.7% EBITDA margin) and trading of goods (steel and other goods sold mainly outside India; 19%, ~5% margin). The engine takes one growth rate and one margin, so the two-line build is kept in lineBuild and checked against model revenue and EBITDA in BELRISE.ctx.js. Share count and Mar-26 balance sheet are pro forma for the Jul-2026 QIP (BELRISE.patch.js). The pending merger of the two promoter companies (BAPL, EITSPL) is NOT in the base: it still needed NCLT approval on 30-Sep-2026 (shown as a sensitivity). Valued on P/E, as the street does.
assumptions._revenueWhy: Sum of the two lines in lineBuild. Manufacturing +18% / +16% / +15%: Q1FY27 +20% (Q4FY26 +21%); orders won in FY26-27 start in Q2-Q4FY27 (exhaust and fuel tank for a fast-growing 2W/3W OEM ~Rs90 cr a year, chassis Rs65 cr and Rs50 cr, solar-tracker assemblies up to Rs150 cr at peak, a 4W EV localisation programme, brakes and suspensions); the Hyva tipper business (bought for Rs54 cr, closing Q3FY27) adds from H2; 4W/CV doubling target. Trading -3% / +5% / +5%: Q1FY27 -19% (Middle East disruption), management expects recovery but slower than manufacturing. Management guidance: mid-teens revenue growth (May and Aug-2026 calls).

assumptions._marginWhy: Blended from lineBuild. Manufacturing 13.2% in FY27 (Q1 12.7%: steel and polymer cost lag, the April wage increments and minimum-wage hike, staff hired ahead of four new plants; management says the cost pain is behind it and margins rise in the coming quarters), 13.5% / 13.6% in FY28-29 as new plants fill and SDM (France) turns EBITDA positive, still below FY25's 13.9%. Trading 4.5% (FY25 6.1%, FY26 5.4%, Q1FY27 4.0%). Group margin 11.8% in FY27 vs 12.1% in FY26: in line with JM Financial (11.8%) and with management's 'broadly stable' guidance only if trading stays small.
assumptions._capexWhy: Guidance: capex 6-6.5% of manufacturing revenue (Q4FY26 call, incl. R&D). 6.25% of our manufacturing revenue plus Rs54 cr for the Hyva tipper business in FY27. FY26 capex Rs486 cr (company), Rs618 cr of fixed assets purchased in the cash-flow statement. Further acquisitions from the QIP money (management intends to deploy most of it in FY27) are not modelled: targets and prices are unknown.
assumptions._depWhy: FY26 depreciation Rs361 cr = 6.9% of average gross block (Rs5,210 cr); Q1FY27 Rs99 cr (~Rs395 cr annualised).
assumptions._treasuryWhy: Applied by the engine to net cash (cash + investments - borrowings incl. leases). cover.headline: A well-run two-wheeler parts maker priced for a story it has not yet written: we initiate with SELL
cover.lead: Belrise Industries (formerly Badve Engineering) makes chassis, exhaust systems, fuel tanks and other metal and plastic parts, mainly for two-wheelers (82% of manufacturing revenue). Revenue grew 15% a year over FY22-26; the May-2025 IPO repaid debt and profit rose 40% in FY26. Since then the founder's family has sold down, the company has raised ₹1,700 cr in a QIP for acquisitions (aerospace, cars and trucks), and the share price has risen 2.7x from the ₹90 IPO price. We forecast EPS of ₹6.38 / ₹7.83 / ₹9.29 for FY27-29E on the post-QIP share count. The street values Belrise on **P/E on FY28E EPS** (Jefferies and JM Financial 26x). The house rule (its own forward P/E median over the 12 months to 30-Sep-2026, 28.1x, cut by the 6.3% same-window auto-component de-rating) gives **26.5x Sep-28E EPS of ₹8.56 = {{dcf.tp|inr}} ({{dcf.upside|chg}}): we initiate with SELL.** Cross-checks: EV/EBITDA ₹181; DCF ₹110. Bull {{scen.bull.tp|inr}}; bear {{scen.bear.tp|inr}}.

arguments.h: A good operator in a slow market
arguments.p: Belrise has out-grown two-wheeler volumes for a decade (revenue >11.5% a year over FY16-25 vs 1.4% for domestic 2W volumes) by adding parts per bike: content per vehicle rose from ~₹12,000 to ~₹20,000 in 18 months (including the promoter companies being merged). Manufacturing margins are steady at 13.7-13.9%, plants are highly automated (890+ robots) and it is now winning business at the two fast-growing 2W makers where it was small (already a ~₹200 cr a year run-rate at one of them). We model manufacturing revenue +{{as.lineBuild.mfgGrowth.0|pct0}} / +{{as.lineBuild.mfgGrowth.1|pct0}} / +{{as.lineBuild.mfgGrowth.2|pct0}}.

arguments.h: But the numbers are less than they look
arguments.p: 19% of revenue is trading of goods at a ~5% margin (−19% in Q1FY27); the largest customer is losing share, so Q1FY27 2W/3W revenue grew 18% against industry production of 20-25%; Q1 margin fell 90bp; ROCE is 14-15%. The FY26 profit jump came from the IPO repaying debt and will not repeat. Our EPS grows ~22% a year over FY26-29E (pro forma for the QIP), helped by interest on the QIP cash.

arguments.h: The new stories are small, early and bought
arguments.p: Aerospace and defence (Chester Hall in the UK, SDM in France, an alliance with Israel's Plasan Sasa), US solar-tracker parts and tipper bodies (Hyva) together are a few per cent of revenue today; SDM lost ₹9.5 cr in its first quarter. Management wants aerospace and defence at 10% of revenue and will spend most of the ₹1,657 cr of net QIP money on acquisitions in FY27: we do not model deals we cannot see.

arguments.h: Valuation: full for a 14% ROCE business
arguments.p: At ₹240.36 the stock trades at 30.7x our FY28E and 28.1x Sep-28E EPS, in the upper part of its 23.5-32.6x range over the last year, while auto-component peers trade 6.3% below their own 12-month medians. The street (targets ₹250-280) includes the pending merger of two promoter companies (+8.2% to our Sep-28E EPS if completed; NCLT approval was still awaited on 30-Sep-2026) and more growth than we do. The DCF (₹110) is far below the price.

catalysts: Q2FY27 results (due by mid-November 2026): whether the Q1 steel and wage costs were passed on, trading recovered, and the new 2W/3W programmes started.
NCLT approval of the BAPL/EITSPL merger: adds ~₹112 cr of profit (FY25) for 4.72 cr new shares; would lift our EPS by ~8%.
Use of the QIP money: management intends to deploy most of ₹1,657 cr in FY27, mainly acquisitions; price paid and earnings acquired decide whether this adds value.
Start of production in Q4FY27: exhaust/fuel tank/chassis for a fast-growing 2W/3W OEM, a top OEM's 2W chassis, US solar-tracker assemblies, 3W brakes.
Hyva tipper business closing (Q3FY27) and the aero-engine localisation talks management mentioned in Aug-2026.

sections.title: A metal-bashing, robot-heavy supplier to two-wheeler makers, plus a trading arm

blocks.p: Belrise cuts, bends, presses, welds, coats and assembles steel into parts that hold a vehicle together: two-wheeler chassis (frames), exhaust systems, fuel tanks, stands, body-in-white (BIW) panels, and for cars and trucks high-tensile chassis members and cross-car beams. It also moulds plastic parts (fenders, cowls), and has started proprietary products: shock absorbers and front forks, steering columns, brakes and filters. 27 plants in 13 cities, 10 states, 3 countries (Q1FY27 deck); 890+ robots; 90,000+ tpa fabrication; 450+ presses up to 1,200 t. It sells to 38 OEMs; exports are only 5.5% of manufacturing revenue. Management stresses that 73.4% of manufacturing revenue is "powertrain-agnostic" (a chassis is needed whether the bike is petrol or electric); exhausts and fuel tanks (~25%) are not.

sections.title: Thirty years as a family supplier to one big customer; in eighteen months: IPO, five acquisitions, a promoter merger and a QIP

blocks.p: Shrikant Badve built the business (as Badve Engineering) around one large two-wheeler customer; the MD said on the Q4FY26 call that the company was once "almost entirely dependent on a single customer". Diversification came through new customers (four added in FY25-26), cars and trucks, and purchases. The pace has picked up sharply since the IPO: H-One India (Mar-2025), Chester Hall and SDM (aerospace, FY26), Hyva's tipper business (signed Aug-2026), and the merger of two promoter-owned companies that supply the same customers.

sections.title: Two-wheelers: a mature market lifted by the GST cut; content per vehicle is where suppliers grow

blocks.p: Belrise sells mainly to two-wheeler makers (82% of FY26 manufacturing revenue). Two-wheeler demand recovered in FY26 after the GST rate cut of late 2025; an analyst on the Q1FY27 call put 2W/3W industry production growth at 20-25% against Belrise's +18%. Over FY16-25 Belrise grew revenue >11.5% a year while domestic 2W industry volumes grew 1.4% a year (company deck, from the prospectus): growth came from content per vehicle and new customers, not the market.

bullets: **Content per vehicle:** 2W content per vehicle ~₹12,000 18 months ago, ~₹20,000 including the two promoter companies being merged (Q4FY26 call); premium-bike chassis worth ~2.2x a commuter chassis (deck).

**Competition:** Sheet-metal, chassis and exhaust supply is fragmented; peers include JBM Auto, Minda Corp, Uno Minda (some products), Endurance (suspension, brakes) and many unlisted vendors. Belrise claims ~24% of Indian 2W metal components (CRISIL, FY24).

**Premiumisation and EVs:** premium bikes need costlier chassis and stainless exhausts; electric two-wheelers keep the chassis and suspension but drop the exhaust and fuel tank (~25% of Belrise's manufacturing revenue is ICE-only).

**Pricing:** parts are made to the vehicle maker's drawing; steel is passed through "back to back" with a lag of a quarter or so (Q1FY27 call). Suppliers earn a conversion margin, not a material margin.
**Cars and trucks:** lightweighting pushes high-tensile steel (H-One can press up to 1,470 MPa, ~3x what is common in India, per the Q1FY27 call); EV makers are localising body parts.

blocks.callout: **So what:** the market Belrise mostly serves grows in single digits over a cycle. A supplier like Belrise grows faster only by adding parts per vehicle and new customers, which it has done; but its biggest customer's share of the two-wheeler market now matters as much as the market itself.

sections.title: Two-wheelers: 82% of manufacturing revenue; growing, but behind the industry while the largest customer loses share

blocks.p: Two- and three-wheeler parts brought in ₹6,340 cr in FY26 (+13.4%) and ₹1,789 cr in Q1FY27 (+18%). Belrise makes the chassis, exhaust, fuel tank, stands, foot rests and other metal parts, and increasingly suspensions and brakes. Content per two-wheeler rose 60-65% in FY25-26 (from ~₹12,000 to ~₹20,000 including the merging promoter companies), ~80% of it from in-house ("proprietary") products, per management. Two problems: the customer it grew up with has been losing market share to "a couple of OEMs who we do not work closely with right now" (Q1FY27 call), and electric bikes need no exhaust or fuel tank.

sections.title: Cars and trucks: +35-37% in FY26 on the H-One purchase; still only 13% of manufacturing revenue

blocks.p: Passenger-vehicle revenue was ₹400 cr in FY26 (+37.0%) and commercial vehicles ₹645 cr (+34.6%); in Q1FY27 ₹101 cr (+22%) and ₹188 cr (+16%). Most of the step-up came from H-One India (93% bought in Mar-2025 from a Japanese listed parent): high-tensile pressings and complex tools for Japanese car makers, plus a technology agreement with H-One Japan (concluded in Q1FY27) for steel up to 1,470 MPa. Management targets a doubling of 4W/CV revenue over two years. New: long members for heavy trucks (Pune), the 59-assembly localisation order for an Indian commercial EV (with tooling and automation, a new revenue line), and Hyva's tipper-body business (three plants, supplying all five big truck makers), bought for ~₹54 cr at ~3.6x EV/EBITDA, closing in Q3FY27.

bullets: **Chester Hall (UK, bought Q4FY26):** precision machining of aero-engine and aerostructure parts in titanium and aluminium for the world's largest aircraft maker and a French engine maker; single-source on several programmes. CY25 revenue ~GBP18.5m, EBITDA GBP2.1-2.2m, price GBP13.2m (~6x EV/EBITDA). Management is in "advanced discussion" to localise high-volume aero-engine parts in India.
**SDM (France):** bought for EUR0.35m (FY27E revenue EUR3-4m); one-time loss of ₹9.5 cr in Q4FY26 on machinery overhaul, legal and staff costs; EBITDA positive expected in 2027.
**Defence:** an alliance with Israel's Plasan Sasa (armoured vehicles); parts already exported to Israel, progress "gradual"; empanelled with one Israeli and two Indian defence makers.
**Solar trackers (US customer):** sheet-metal assemblies for ~2.5 GW a year, from Q4FY27, up to ~₹150 cr a year at peak.
**Target:** aerospace and defence at least 10% of revenue in the medium term, mostly through acquisitions funded by the QIP.

blocks.p: **Trading of goods** was ₹1,775 cr in FY26 (+4.6%) at a 5.4% EBITDA margin (FY25 6.1%), and fell 19% to ₹349 cr in Q1FY27 as the Middle East conflict disrupted demand and shipping. We model ₹1,721 / 1,807 / 1,898 cr at 4.5%. It adds revenue but little value; a further decline would lower revenue growth but raise the reported margin.

blocks.callout: **So what:** investors are already paying for the aerospace story (the stock re-rated when the deals were announced). On the numbers, these units together are perhaps 3-5% of manufacturing revenue, partly loss-making, and their growth depends on deals not yet done. We give them no value beyond what is in our forecasts.

blocks.callout: **Honest verdict: no durable moat.** Belrise is a well-automated, vertically integrated build-to-print supplier with long relationships, which gives it cost and quality advantages and sticky programmes. It does not own the design of most of what it makes, passes steel through at cost, and earns a ROCE of ~15%. The proprietary products and high-tensile technology could build a moat over time; today they are small.

sections.title: Revenue +15% a year since FY22; the margin slipped from 14% to 12%, and the IPO cut interest so profit jumped 40% in FY26

blocks.p: Belrise's consolidated revenue rose from ₹5,397 cr in FY22 to ₹9,509 cr in FY26, 15% a year; ₹1,775 cr of FY26 revenue (19%) is trading of goods, mostly steel and other materials sold to buyers outside India at a ~5% margin, so manufacturing revenue was ₹7,735 cr. The EBITDA margin fell from 14.0% to 12.1% as the trading share rose and raw materials went from 78% to 81% of revenue (Screener cost split; materials include the goods traded). Depreciation rose from ₹246 cr to ₹361 cr with new plants and H-One (bought in Mar-2025). For three years profit hardly moved (₹314 cr in FY23 and FY24, ₹355 cr in FY25) because interest took ₹250-307 cr a year; the IPO repaid ₹1,596 cr of debt in Jun-2025, interest fell to ₹232 cr and profit rose 40% to ₹497 cr in FY26.

sections.title: Capital hungry: ₹2,677 cr of capex in five years against ₹3,425 cr of operating cash; ₹3,850 cr of new equity since May-2025

blocks.p: Over FY22-26 Belrise generated ₹3,425 cr of operating cash (before interest), spent ₹2,677 cr on fixed assets and paid ₹51 cr of dividends. After ~₹1,300 cr of interest over the five years, little was left: debt rose to ₹2,964 cr by Mar-2025. Since then the company has raised ₹2,150 cr in the IPO (May-2025, at ₹90) and ₹1,700 cr in a QIP (Jul-2026, at ₹220). Management guides capex at 6-6.5% of manufacturing revenue (incl. R&D) and wants to spend most of the QIP money on acquisitions in FY27, mainly aerospace abroad and car/truck parts in India. Returns are modest: ROCE 14-15% on Screener's basis (company ROACE 14.7% in FY26), about our 12.5% cost of equity.

bullets: **Comparability.** FY25 includes H-One only from 28-Mar-2025 (consolidated from FY26); Chester Hall and SDM join in Q4FY26; Hyva from Q3FY27; and the BAPL/EITSPL merger, once approved, will restate the numbers. Like-for-like growth is not disclosed.

**Other income.** ₹110 cr in FY26: interest ₹45 cr (IPO money before debt repayment), "miscellaneous" ₹53 cr (not explained in the notes) and FX gains ₹11 cr. Other income was 16% of FY26 pre-tax profit. Q1FY27 ₹18 cr.

sections.title: Our honest summary: a good operator at 28.1x Sep-28E EPS; SELL on price, not on the business

blocks.callout: **What you are buying:** a well-automated, vertically integrated maker of chassis, exhausts and other metal parts for India's two-wheeler makers, steadily adding parts per vehicle and new customers, now debt-free with ₹1,657 cr of fresh cash. You are also buying a family-controlled company in a hurry: four acquisitions in eighteen months, a related-party merger, a fifth of revenue in low-margin trading and plans to spend the QIP money on aerospace deals.

**What you are paying:** 37.7x our FY27E and 30.7x FY28E EPS for ~22% a year EPS growth and a ~15% ROCE. Over the last year the market paid a median 28.1x forward; today it pays 30.7x, near the top of the range, while auto-component peers have de-rated. The street's targets (median ₹270) assume the merger and more growth.

assumptions._note: GAM Research forecast drivers for Belrise Industries (consolidated; Rs crore). Revenue has two lines with very different margins: manufacturing (sheet-metal, chassis, exhaust, polymer, suspension and other parts; 81% of FY26 revenue, 13.7% EBITDA margin) and trading of goods (steel and other goods sold mainly outside India; 19%, ~5% margin). The engine takes one growth rate and one margin, so the two-line build is kept in lineBuild and checked against model revenue and EBITDA in BELRISE.ctx.js. Share count and Mar-26 balance sheet are pro forma for the Jul-2026 QIP (BELRISE.patch.js). The pending merger of the two promoter companies (BAPL, EITSPL) is NOT in the base: it still needed NCLT approval on 30-Sep-2026 (shown as a sensitivity). Valued on P/E, as the street does.
assumptions._revenueWhy: Sum of the two lines in lineBuild. Manufacturing +18% / +16% / +15%: Q1FY27 +20% (Q4FY26 +21%); orders won in FY26-27 start in Q2-Q4FY27 (exhaust and fuel tank for a fast-growing 2W/3W OEM ~Rs90 cr a year, chassis Rs65 cr and Rs50 cr, solar-tracker assemblies up to Rs150 cr at peak, a 4W EV localisation programme, brakes and suspensions); the Hyva tipper business (bought for Rs54 cr, closing Q3FY27) adds from H2; 4W/CV doubling target. Trading -3% / +5% / +5%: Q1FY27 -19% (Middle East disruption), management expects recovery but slower than manufacturing. Management guidance: mid-teens revenue growth (May and Aug-2026 calls).

lineBuild._why: FY26 from the Q4FY26 presentation (p7-8, 16): manufacturing revenue Rs7,734.6 cr (EBITDA Rs1,057.7 cr, 13.7%), trading Rs1,774.5 cr (EBITDA Rs96.1 cr = total Rs1,153.8 cr less manufacturing), total Rs9,509.1 cr. Q1FY27: manufacturing Rs2,197.9 cr at 12.7%, trading Rs348.6 cr at 4.0%.

assumptions._marginWhy: Blended from lineBuild. Manufacturing 13.2% in FY27 (Q1 12.7%: steel and polymer cost lag, the April wage increments and minimum-wage hike, staff hired ahead of four new plants; management says the cost pain is behind it and margins rise in the coming quarters), 13.5% / 13.6% in FY28-29 as new plants fill and SDM (France) turns EBITDA positive, still below FY25's 13.9%. Trading 4.5% (FY25 6.1%, FY26 5.4%, Q1FY27 4.0%). Group margin 11.8% in FY27 vs 12.1% in FY26: in line with JM Financial (11.8%) and with management's 'broadly stable' guidance only if trading stays small.
assumptions._capexWhy: Guidance: capex 6-6.5% of manufacturing revenue (Q4FY26 call, incl. R&D). 6.25% of our manufacturing revenue plus Rs54 cr for the Hyva tipper business in FY27. FY26 capex Rs486 cr (company), Rs618 cr of fixed assets purchased in the cash-flow statement. Further acquisitions from the QIP money (management intends to deploy most of it in FY27) are not modelled: targets and prices are unknown.
assumptions._depWhy: FY26 depreciation Rs361 cr = 6.9% of average gross block (Rs5,210 cr); Q1FY27 Rs99 cr (~Rs395 cr annualised).
assumptions._treasuryWhy: Applied by the engine to net cash (cash + investments - borrowings incl. leases). Pro forma Mar-26 net cash ~Rs1,090 cr after the Rs1,657 cr net QIP proceeds (net debt Rs598 cr before it). Bank deposits / liquid funds ~6.5%. Includes Rs113 cr of unlisted equity investments (Rs99 cr in BAPL) that earn nothing: overstates other income by ~Rs7 cr a year.
assumptions._otherIncomeWhy: Non-treasury other income: FY26 Rs110 cr = interest Rs45 cr (IPO cash parked before the Jun-2025 debt repayment), miscellaneous Rs53 cr (incl. scrap and incentives), FX gain Rs11 cr, rent Rs1 cr (AR FY26 note 28). Q1FY27 Rs18 cr; the four quarters to Jun-2026 Rs99 cr. Rs55 cr in FY27 (Q1 plus ~Rs12 cr a quarter), Rs50 cr after; FX gains not repeated.
assumptions._interestWhy: FY26 Rs232 cr (IPO repaid Rs1,596 cr of debt in Jun-2025); Q1FY27 Rs46 cr on ~Rs1,500 cr of gross debt incl. leases and bill discounting. Part of the QIP repays debt (Rs532 cr deployed by 30-Sep-2026, mainly debt repayment and vendor payments, per CRISIL): ~Rs43 cr a quarter from Q2.
assumptions._taxWhy: FY26 effective 25.4% (Rs169 cr on Rs666 cr), Q1FY27 26.9%; new regime 25.17% plus some non-deductible items.
assumptions._payoutWhy: FY26 final dividend Rs0.55 a share (~Rs49 cr on 89 cr shares, ~10% of profit; Screener payout 10%). First dividend as a listed company; no stated policy.

dcf._betaWhy: Two-wheeler-heavy auto supplier (82% of manufacturing revenue), cyclical, with net cash after the QIP: beta 1.0, cost of equity 12.5%, used as the discount rate.
dcf._tgWhy: Indian vehicle production ~5-6% plus content gains; house range 5-6%: 6%.
dcf._fadeGrowthWhy: Revenue growth fades from ~13.5% in FY29E to 8%.
dcf._fadeMarginWhy: Group EBITDA margin drifts to 12.5% as trading shrinks in the mix.
dcf._fadeCapexWhy: Capex ~5% of total revenue (6-6.5% of manufacturing revenue) in the long run; depreciation ~3.8% of revenue (FY26 3.8%).
